subject.title: fix(telegram): polling worker pins a CPU core when the Bot API answers empty getUpdates instantly

question: Should Telegram polling use a fixed one-second delay after every fast empty successful poll, accepting up to one second of additional idle-to-first-update latency on non-long-polling endpoints?
rationale: The patch correctly prevents the demonstrated busy loop, but the interval is a user-visible message-delivery policy for self-hosted Bot API and proxy deployments rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Accept the one-second bound
options.body: Merge the patch with the explicit policy that fast-empty endpoints are limited to one poll per second while idle.

options.title: Adopt adaptive pacing instead
options.body: Request an owner-defined backoff or wake-up design that reduces spin without imposing the same fixed first-update delay.

recommendation.title: Accept the one-second bound
recommendation.body: Merge the patch with the explicit policy that fast-empty endpoints are limited to one poll per second while idle.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied evidence ties this contributor directly to the observed deployment behavior, though a current-main Telegram history owner should make the final policy decision.
